pages.title: The Tortoise and the Hare: Slow and Steady
bulletPoints: A boastful speedy Hare teased a quiet little Tortoise for walking so slowly through the forest meadow.
The challenge: Tortoise proposed a cross-forest race to the old grandfather oak tree.
The Hare’s mistake: Racing far ahead, Hare grew overconfident and took a nap under the warm apple tree shade.
The triumph: Step by steady step, Tortoise never stopped, crossing the finish line just as Hare woke up in disbelief!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Slow and steady wins the race.

pages.title: The Lion and the Mouse: Kindness is Never Wasted
bulletPoints: A mighty Lion slept in the sun when a tiny field mouse scurried across his giant paws.
The plea: Lion trapped Mouse under his claw; Mouse begged for mercy, promising to help Lion one day.
The Lion chuckled and let the little mouse go free, amused by the idea of a mouse helping a king.
The rescue: Days later, Lion was caught in hunters' ropes; Mouse heard his roars and gnawed through the thick cords!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Even the smallest friend can be of great help.

pages.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf: Protecting Your Word
bulletPoints: A shepherd boy tended his village flock on the hillside and grew lonely and bored.
The false alarm: He shouted "Wolf! Wolf!" causing all the villagers to drop their work and run up the hill.
Laughing at their alarm, he repeated the prank again the following afternoon, delighting in the commotion.
The real wolf: A hungry gray wolf truly emerged from the dark woods; the boy cried for help, but nobody believed him.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Nobody believes a liar, even when they speak the truth.

pages.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper: Seasons of Work
bulletPoints: All summer long, Grasshopper sang, danced, and rested in the warm green meadow sunshine.
Nearby, busy little Ant carried heavy grains of golden wheat on his back to his underground pantry.
"Why work so hard?" asked Grasshopper. "Winter is coming," replied Ant, "and winter is cold and barren."
When freezing snow blankets fell, Grasshopper shivered with no food, while Ant’s family ate warm roasted corn.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Prepare today for the needs of tomorrow.

pages.title: The North Wind and the Sun: Gentle Persuasion
bulletPoints: The North Wind and the Sun argued over who was stronger in the celestial realm.
The challenge: Whichever could make a walking traveler take off his warm woolen cloak would be crowned champion.
The Wind’s attempt: Wind blew fierce icy gales, but the traveler only wrapped his cloak tighter around his shoulders.
The Sun’s turn: Sun beamed warm, pleasant golden rays; within minutes, the traveler grew warm and cheerfully took off his coat.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Warmth and gentle kindness achieve what harsh force never can.

pages.title: The Crow and the Pitcher: Wit Over Despair
bulletPoints: A thirsty black Crow flew over dry summer fields searching desperately for a drink of fresh water.
He spotted a clay pitcher, but the water inside was low and his beak could not reach the surface.
Giving up seemed easy, but Crow looked around and spotted small pebbles scattered across the garden path.
One by one, Crow dropped pebbles into the pitcher; slowly, the water level rose until he drank happily!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Thoughtful problem-solving overcomes brute strength.

pages.title: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse: True Peace
bulletPoints: Country Mouse welcomed his cousin Town Mouse to his hollow log home, serving fresh acorns and wheat stalks.
Town Mouse turned his nose up: "Come to my palace in town, where we feast on jellies, cake, and cheese!"
In town, they sneaked into a rich banquet room, but suddenly ferocious barking dogs burst through the doors.
Scampering for his life into a wall crack, Country Mouse whispered: "I prefer my dry acorns in peace to rich cakes in fear!"
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Better a modest life in peace than riches in terror.

pages.title: The Fox and the Grapes: Contentment in Truth
bulletPoints: A hungry Fox strolled through an autumn vineyard and spotted luscious, purple grapes hanging high on a vine.
His mouth watered as sunlight glistened on the plump, juicy fruit dangling just out of reach.
He backed up, sprinted, and leaped into the air, but snapped his jaws on empty breeze.
After trying ten times and missing, he walked away with his nose in the air: "Bah, they are probably sour anyway!"
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: It is easy to despise what you cannot attain.

pages.title: The Golden Goose: Gratitude Over Greed
bulletPoints: A poor woodcutter owned a wonderful white goose that laid one solid golden egg every single morning.
He sold the eggs in the market, quickly becoming wealthy with warm clothes and a fine timber home.
Greed took over: He thought the goose must have a vast treasure of gold inside its belly right now.
He foolishly cut the goose open, only to find it was like any normal bird—and now his daily gift was lost forever.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Greed destroys the very blessings you enjoy.

pages.title: The Ugly Duckling: The Beauty of Becoming
bulletPoints: In a warm farmyard nest, one egg was larger and took longer to hatch into a strange, clumsy gray chick.
The farmyard ducks pecked and teased him because he did not look like the fluffy yellow ducklings.
Heartbroken, he flew away and spent a lonely, freezing winter hiding in the reeds of a mountain marsh.
When spring flowers bloomed, he looked into clear water and saw his reflection: he had grown into a majestic white Swan!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Do not judge by appearances; true greatness takes time to unfold.

pages.title: The Three Little Pigs: Diligence and Resilience
bulletPoints: Three pig brothers set out into the world to build their very own homes.
First pig built quickly with yellow straw; second pig built with light wooden sticks so they could play.
The third pig worked patiently all day, laying solid clay bricks and mortar to build a sturdy home.
The Big Bad Wolf huffed and puffed down the straw and stick shacks, but could not budge the brick house!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Hard work and patience build lasting security.

pages.title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears: Respecting Boundaries
bulletPoints: A curious girl with golden curls walked through the forest and discovered an unlocked cottage.
Three bowls of porridge: Papa Bear’s too hot, Mama Bear’s too cold, and Baby Bear’s just right—which she ate all up.
She broke Baby Bear’s little chair, and fell fast asleep across Baby Bear’s cozy bed.
When the three bears returned from their walk, Goldilocks awoke to three furry faces and leaped out the window!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Always respect others' homes and personal belongings.

pages.title: The Elves and the Shoemaker: Quiet Generosity
bulletPoints: An honest old shoemaker had only enough leather left to stitch one final pair of shoes before bed.
In the morning, he awoke to find exquisite, perfect shoes stitched with invisible, delicate seams.
A customer bought them for double the price; the next night, two pairs were completed with matching mastery.
Shoemaker and his wife hid behind a curtain and saw two tiny shivering elves; in gratitude, they stitched warm coats for them!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Generosity and gratitude create endless joy.

pages.title: Jack and the Beanstalk: Courage and Wonder
bulletPoints: Poor Jack traded his family's only milk cow for five shiny, colorful magic beans.
His angry mother tossed them out the kitchen window, but overnight they sprouted into a colossal green beanstalk.
Jack climbed past the clouds into a sky kingdom where a giant kept a golden harp and a hen that laid golden eggs.
With quick wits and nimble feet, Jack carried the hen home and chopped down the stalk just in time!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Have the courage to climb toward your highest dreams.

pages.title: The Little Red Hen: Pitching In to Share
bulletPoints: Little Red Hen found grains of wheat and asked: "Who will help me plant these seeds in the soil?"
"Not I," barked the lazy dog; "Not I," purred the sleepy cat; "Not I," quacked the idle duck.
"Then I will," said Hen; she watered the wheat, harvested the stalks, and ground them into fine white flour.
When the fragrance of freshly baked warm bread filled the air, all animals begged to eat; Hen shared it with her working chicks!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Those who help do the work deserve to share the rewards.

pages.title: The Fisherman and His Wife: Contentment with Enough
bulletPoints: A humble fisherman caught an enchanted golden flounder that pleaded for its life and offered wishes.
The kind fisherman released the fish without asking for anything in return, returning to his tiny thatched hut.
His ambitious wife sent him back to demand a cottage, then a stone castle, then to be crowned king.
When she demanded to control the sun and moon, the sea raged black, and they found themselves back in their humble hut.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Never let endless wanting drown out gratitude for what you have.

pages.title: The Steadfast Tin Soldier: Unshakable Loyalty
bulletPoints: Cast from an old tin spoon, one brave little toy soldier had only one leg, yet stood tall and proud.
He admired a graceful paper dancer standing on one tiptoe outside her cardboard castle.
Tossed by winds onto a paper boat down stormy street gutters and swallowed by a fish, he never dropped his musket.
Recovered back in his home parlor, he stood steadfast beside his dancer, proving courage shines forever.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: True loyalty and courage never waver, whatever storms arise.

pages.title: The Princess and the Pea: Inner Sensitivity
bulletPoints: A prince sought a true princess of authentic refinement and tender sensitivity.
On a stormy night, a drenched maiden knocked at the castle gate claiming to be a royal princess.
The queen placed a tiny green pea on the bedstead and piled twenty thick mattresses and featherbeds on top.
In the morning, the maiden confessed she had tossed all night bruised by something hard—proving her true royal sensitivity!
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: True nobility is revealed through genuine sensitivity and truth.

pages.title: Rumpelstiltskin: The Power of Truth and Names
bulletPoints: A miller foolishly bragged to the king that his clever daughter could spin yellow straw into pure gold thread.
A mysterious little man appeared in the locked tower, spinning straw into gold in exchange for her necklace and ring.
For the final room, she promised her firstborn child unless she could discover the little man’s secret name.
Her royal messenger overheard him singing around a midnight campfire: "Merrily feast, for Rumpelstiltskin is my name!"
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Truth and resourcefulness unravel even the deepest secrets.

pages.title: The Magic Paintbrush: Art to Lift the World
bulletPoints: A kind orphan boy named Ma Liang loved drawing pictures in the dirt with broken sticks.
An elder gifted him a golden paintbrush that brought everything he painted into living reality.
Ma Liang painted buffaloes for poor farmers to plow fields, water wheels for drought villages, and food for the hungry.
When a greedy emperor demanded piles of gold, Ma Liang painted an ocean and a ship, sailing away into freedom.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Moral: Talents should be used with compassion to bring joy and justice to others.
